name: A Jackson, Mississippi street

place_source.title: Wikidata: Jackson, Mississippi (Q28198), coordinate location and elevation above sea level

blurb: A Jackson, Mississippi street under a broad shade canopy: southern magnolia and willow oak over front yards of crape myrtle, redbud and hackberry, where cardinals and mockingbirds hold the wires, gray squirrels work the trunks, and opossums and raccoons cross the wet verge after rain.

facts.text: Jackson lies in the humid subtropical climate zone (Koppen Cfa). Rain falls all year, winter and spring are the wettest seasons, September and October the driest, and snow is rare.

source.title: Wikipedia: Jackson, Mississippi

facts.text: Average annual precipitation in Jackson is 57.35 inches, and much of it arrives in thunderstorms; thunder is heard on roughly 70 days each year.

source.title: Wikipedia: Jackson, Mississippi
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Jackson, Mississippi", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Jackson's record high is 107 degrees Fahrenheit and its record low minus 5, so a summer scene can be genuinely hot and a winter one genuinely cold.

source.title: Wikipedia: Jackson, Mississippi
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Jackson, Mississippi", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The city sits primarily in northeastern Hinds County, and the Pearl River forms most of its eastern border.

facts.text: The Choctaw name for the wooded area where Jackson stands today was Chisha Foka, meaning "Among the post oaks".

facts.text: Jackson's 2020 census population was 153,701, with a median age of 36.4 years, and 99.6 percent of residents lived in urban areas.
